title: Egress and transaction charges: why reading can cost more than storing

videos.script: Most people price a storage account by its size. That is one meter of four, and often the smallest. {{meters}} Every operation has a price, whatever its size. Every byte that leaves the region has a price too. Capacity is only what the account costs while nobody touches it. {{count}} In this lesson a short program counts its own requests. Six thousand taps from Quitanda's app, written a blob each, are six thousand writes. The same taps as one file are one. And one large file can be twenty-one. {{small}} Then a second program prices five designs, with round numbers that say they are illustrative. Reading the taps every morning costs a hundred and sixty times storing them. Moving them to the cool tier makes it worse, not better. {{internet}} Then Quitanda's product images, served to the internet. The transfer is nearly the whole bill. {{inside}} And the traffic that never leaves Azure. A NAT gateway charges for every gigabyte on its way to the account next door. One free setting on the subnet takes that line off the bill. {{payer}}
